title: Salvation and Grace - Episode 5: Eternal Intercession Saving Souls Completely

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome to Salvation and Grace. <chuckle> I'm Sarah Mitchell. <short pause> Tonight we're asking a question: how completely does Jesus save you?

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: The writer of Hebrews gives us an answer that reaches all the way to this very moment, as you lie here in the quiet.
Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Three words stand at the heart of this promise: to the uttermost.

The phrase means completely, fully, forever. <short pause> Jesus saves you not partially, not temporarily, but all the way through. <short pause> This isn't a salvation that covers only part of your life or part of your need. <short pause> It reaches from the moment you first believed to this night, and onward to the last day of your life and beyond.

Now notice what makes this complete salvation possible. <short pause> The verse says he ever lives to make intercession. <short pause> Jesus is not a savior who did his work and walked away. <short pause> He lives right now, and his life has a purpose: he is praying for you.

In the ancient temple, a high priest would enter the holy place to intercede for the people, but his work was never finished. <short pause> He would have to return again and again, year after year. <short pause> But Jesus entered once, and he remains there, alive and interceding without end.
This means that at this very hour, Jesus is presenting you before the Father. <short pause> He is speaking on your behalf, holding up the worth of his own sacrifice as the reason you are accepted.
Your standing before God does not rest on how well you prayed today or how strong your faith felt. <short pause> It rests on him, on his unending life and unceasing prayer.
Think of the ones who come to God by him. <short pause> That phrase describes every believer. <short pause> If you have come to the Father through Jesus, this promise is yours.
You did not come because you were strong or worthy. <short pause> You came because he made a way, and he keeps that way open every moment.
The word intercession means to plead for another, to stand in the gap.

When your own prayers feel weak or wordless, he is praying. <short pause> When you are too tired to form a thought, he is interceding. <short pause> When guilt whispers that you have failed too many times, his voice before the Father is stronger than any accusation.
Earlier in this same letter, the writer describes Jesus as a high priest who is touched with the feeling of our infirmities.
For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. <long pause>

He knows what it is to be human. <short pause> He knows weariness and sorrow and the weight of a long day. <short pause> And so his prayers for you are not distant or abstract. <short pause> They are informed by true compassion.

This is grace that does not run out. <short pause> You cannot exhaust the intercession of Jesus by needing it too often. <short pause> You cannot wear out his patience or his willingness to present you as his own.
The apostle Paul, writing to the Romans, asked who could bring a charge against God's elect.

Who shall lay any thing to the charge of God’s elect? <short pause> It is God that justifieth. <short pause> Who is he that condemneth? <short pause> It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us. <long pause>
The answer is no one. <short pause> No accusation can stand, because Christ has died and risen and now sits at the right hand of God, interceding.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So what does this mean for you tonight, as you let go of the day? <short pause> It means you can rest in a salvation that does not depend on you holding on tightly. <exhales> Jesus holds you.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: It means that the mistakes you made today, the words you wish you could take back, the patience you lost, none of it has moved you outside his care. <short pause> He is praying for you still.

It means you are not saved only up to a point, only as far as your strength could carry you. <short pause> You are saved to the uttermost, completely, held by a savior who will never stop interceding.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: You do not have to lie here wondering if you have done enough or been enough. <short pause> The question has already been answered by the one who gave himself for you and who lives to present you before the Father. <short pause> Let that truth settle over you now. <short pause> Jesus is praying for you tonight, and his prayers are heard.

Let us pray. <short pause> Father, thank you that Jesus ever lives to intercede for us, and that his salvation reaches all the way to this quiet moment. <short pause> Help us rest in the completeness of what he has done.
Goodnight.
